newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Dolenjska bank 1996 net profit up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dolenjska bank 1996 net profit up 20 pct.

text.p: Slovenian bank Dolenjska Banka on Thursday reported a 20 percent jump in 1996 net profit and forecast a similar increase this year.

Net profit rose to 481.4 million tolars ($3.08 million) from 402.2 million while total assets reached 53.2 billion tolars after 39.7 billion, deputy chief executive Milena Dular said. She forecast a 20 percent increase in assets in 1997.
"The main reason for the rise in profit and balance sheet assets is that we managed to extend our business network throughout Slovenia," Dular told Reuters.
Dolenjska's market share rose to 3.1 percent in 1996 from 2.7 percent.
The bank planned to pay an unchanged dividend of 800 tolars a share, Dular said, adding that 1996 earnings would go towards building reserves.
She was upbeat on prospects for the current year.
"There is still room to extend our business in Slovenia and we plan further growth this year," she said. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
